original_question: Construct non-elementary holomorphic foliations F on Pk with leaves of dimension greater than 1 such that no leaf contains a compact curve.
target_in_paper: Section 10, Problem 10.2: the paper asks to construct non-elementary foliations in \mathbb{P}^k with leaves of dimension larger than 1 such that every leaf does not contain a compact curve.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual problem. It correctly identifies the ambient space \mathbb{P}^k, asks for holomorphic foliations with leaves of complex dimension greater than 1, includes the crucial exclusion of elementary examples via the word "non-elementary," and imposes the paper's universal condition that no leaf contain a compact curve.
missing_details: The paper's problem is in complex projective space \mathbb{P}^k over \mathbb{C}; that field is implicit in the draft.
The surrounding Section 10 context allows foliations to be possibly singular; the draft does not say this explicitly.

The phrase "non-elementary" is not self-contained unless one adds the paper's definition: elementary foliations are those defined by closed forms, or by forms that become closed after multiplication by integrating factors.

The paper gives a codimension-1 clarification that should be recorded if one wants the question to be stand-alone: it excludes logarithmic first-integral examples whose leaves are level sets of multivalued holomorphic functions of the form \prod_i f_i^{\lambda_i} with real exponents \lambda_i.
The quantifier is universal over leaves: the condition is that every leaf contains no compact curve, not merely generic leaves.
To be fully stand-alone, "compact curve" should be understood as a compact complex analytic curve contained in a leaf.
The paper does not impose degree, homogeneity, codimension, or nilpotency restrictions here; a faithful rewrite should not add any such hypotheses.
The nearby context matters: Problem 10.2 is posed as an example-construction problem motivated by the search for an ergodic theory for foliations whose leaves have dimension greater than 1.
refined_question: Can one construct a non-elementary holomorphic foliation, possibly with singularities, in complex projective space \mathbb{P}^k whose leaves have complex dimension strictly larger than 1 and such that no leaf contains a compact complex curve? Here "non-elementary" excludes foliations defined by closed forms and foliations defined by forms that become closed after multiplication by integrating factors; in codimension 1, this in particular excludes the logarithmic first-integral case where the leaves are level sets of multivalued holomorphic functions of the form \prod_i f_i^{\lambda_i} with \lambda_i \in \mathbb{R}.
justification: This paper is a list of numbered open problems rather than a theorem-conjecture-development paper, so the template references to Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 do not apply here. Your draft matches Section 10, Problem 10.2 almost verbatim. The only substantive incompleteness is that the draft does not make the paper's meaning of "non-elementary" explicit, and it leaves implicit the complex setting, the possible presence of singularities, and the universal quantifier over all leaves. The immediate paragraph after Problem 10.2 supplies the hidden exclusion of elementary/logarithmic first-integral examples and notes that the problem is open even in codimension 1, so that nearby context should be folded into the refined stand-alone version.
